conviction_note: The revenue for FY26 was largely pre-released (9M organic +10% against a >9% guide, 29 Jul 2026), so the move sits in what is new: the FY27 first guide, the size of the buyback, margin and FCF. abs_move is 6.5 because this is a scheduled first-guide day and Sage's last four FY-results days moved +7.3/+13.3/+17.9/+1.2. p_up is only 56, from inference: the Q3 exit rate against FY27 consensus, a buyback pattern, a peer guide-raise, and an entry depressed by the 17 Nov AI-software selloff. The weaker FY25 reaction, the 45% rally off the July low and the AI-disruption tape keep it near 50. impact_sum 0.95 and the scaled 0.78 agree in sign and scale.

H1 FY26: underlying op margin 23.9% (+80bps), ARR +11% to £2,727m, renewal rate 102%, FCF £241m (H1 25 £246m); FY26 guide raised to organic growth above 9%
CFO on the Q3 call: margin expansion at the lower end of the 50-100bps range (FY25 margin 23.9%, so about 24.4-24.5% for FY26). Secondary summary only, not confirmed in the transcript
£300m buyback started 2 Mar 2026, expected to complete by 5 Jun 2026; no Transaction in Own Shares RNS since 28 May 2026

new_in_release.expect: FY27 first guide. Consensus is about 9.4% organic total revenue growth (range 8.6-10.5). Sage's habit is '9% or above'. The Q3 exit rate of about 11-12% underlying leaves room for a 10% framing, though that is not confirmed. Lean slightly up.
A new buyback is likely, following the pattern of £400m at the FY24 results and £300m at FY25, and none has run since June. The size is unknown and probably expected.
FY26 organic growth of about 10%, in line with the 9.9% consensus; margin about 24.4-24.5%, inside the guide. About 0.
FY FCF may lag profit growth on tax timing and higher interest, as it did in H1 (£241m vs £246m). Small negative risk.
ARR, renewal rate and evidence that AI is monetising, which will be read through the AI-disruption narrative. Unknown.

findings.finding: Sage has paired every recent full-year result with a new buyback (£400m Nov 2024, £300m Nov 2025). The last £300m programme was due to complete by 5 Jun 2026, and no buyback has run since late May despite cash conversion of 116%, so a new programme at these results is very likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY24 results with a £400m buyback: +17.9%. FY25 results with £300m: +1.2%. The buyback was not the only news on either day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The pattern is visible to all 19 analysts. The unpriced part is the size: six months without a programme and an oversubscribed €500m refinancing in Sep 2026 leave room for a programme above £300m. If the size were priced, there would be a sell-side number for it, and none was found.
findings.independence: The FY25 results RNS shows the same pattern: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sage-group--sge/results-for-the-year-ended-30-september-2025/9242595 . The Investegate company page shows the last Transaction in Own Shares on 2026-05-28: https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/SGE

findings.finding: Revenue growth accelerated through FY26: organic Q1 +10%, 9M +10%, and Q3 total revenue +12% underlying to £699m. FY27 consensus is only 9.4% (range 8.6-10.5), so the FY27 first guide has room to be framed at or above 10% rather than the habitual '9% or above'. This is an inference: management has said nothing about FY27 beyond investing 'for FY27 and beyond'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY-results days, when the first guide comes out: +7.3% (2022), +13.3% (2023), +17.9% (2024), +1.2% (2025, guide '9% or above'). The Q3 FY26 acceleration day: +8.75%. Q1 FY26, also an acceleration: −5.1%, in an AI-fear tape.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus for FY27 (9.4%) sits below FY26's run-rate (about 10% organic, Q3 about 11-12% underlying). If the market expected a 10%+ guide, the company-compiled FY27 consensus would sit at or above 10%. The bar is snippet-only and about six months old, so this finding is capped.
findings.independence: Consensus FY27 +9.2% revenue growth: https://stockanalysis.com/quote/lon/SGE/forecast/ . Peer Xero raised its FY revenue guide on 12 Nov 2026: https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/xero-shares-surge-to-two-month-high-on-1b-buyback

findings.finding: FY26 margin is guided to the lower end of a 50-100bps expansion (FY25 23.9%, so about 24.4%), which implies H2 expansion of only about 20-30bps after H1's +80bps. That is inside the guide and in line with the roughly 24.5% consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26, +80bps margin with the guide raised: −0.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because management said it out loud. The residual is that an FY27 margin guide could again say only 'trend upwards', which is weaker than the 25.2% FY27 consensus implies. Secondary summary only; not confirmed in the transcript.

findings.finding: Peer Xero, which reported its half to 30 Sep 2026 on 12 Nov 2026, raised its full-year revenue guide to about NZ$3.8bn from NZ$3.675bn, added 226k net subscribers and announced an A$1bn buyback. Its shares rose about 6%. Sage rose only about 1% that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of Sage reacting to Xero prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer, not a counterparty, and Xero's geography mix differs (ANZ/UK small business). If the read-through were priced, Sage would have tracked Xero's +6%, not +1%. Sized small because the link is unestablished.

findings.finding: A sector-wide AI-disruption selloff hit software on 17 Nov 2026 (IGV −4.4%, Intuit about −7%, linked partly to Anthropic's Claude personal-finance tool and its pending IPO). Sage fell 3.9% that day with no company news and sits 6.6% below its 5 Nov high going into the print. The release will be read through that narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (27 Jan 2026): revenue accelerated to 10% organic and the stock fell 5.1% in an AI-fear tape, falling a further 9.8% on 3 Feb. Q3 FY26 (29 Jul 2026) came out of a depressed base and rose 8.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: The selloff itself is in the price, since the stock fell. What is not determined is whether the sector tape on 19 Nov keeps pressing; Intuit reports after the US close that day, outside the window. This finding moves both ways, which is why its range is wide around a small negative.

findings.finding: The sell-side is split and the price sits at the consensus target. Canaccord cut to Hold on 26 Oct 2026 on valuation after a rally of more than 45% (target 1,230p), Investec upgraded to Buy (1,300p) on 9 Oct, and Barclays stays Sell at 850p. The average target is 1,148p against a spot of 1,128p.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and therefore priced. It is filed only because it is a sourced fact; it says there is no valuation cushion if the guide is merely in line.

findings.finding: Sage redeemed its €500m 3.820% notes due Feb 2028 at the make-whole amount on 28 Sep 2026, inside FY26, funded by a €500m 4.2805% 2032 bond that was more than five times oversubscribed. This means a non-underlying make-whole cost in statutory finance costs and slightly higher run-rate interest.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small. It sits below operating income with no path to the guide; the money buys a maturity extension, not distress.

findings.finding: H1 FY26 free cash flow was flat at £241m (H1 25 £246m) despite operating cash flow up 15%, because of tax-payment timing and higher net interest on new debt. FY FCF may print below profit growth, a cash line that can weigh on an otherwise in-line release.
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 number is public and the company explained it as timing, so most of it is known. The residual is whether H2 recovers it. No consensus FCF figure was found.

outside_window.finding: Intuit reports fiscal Q1 FY27 after the US close on 19 Nov 2026, after the LSE close that ends this window, so its read-through lands on 20 Nov

baseline_tension: The lean is mildly positive (+0.72, driven by the short-squeeze component of a flat 1.0% short), and the findings agree in sign but are inference-led. The 20-day (−2.4%) and 5-day (−2.8%) run-ups are negative because of the 17 Nov sector selloff, while the stock is about +37% since July, so the free control and the findings point slightly the same way (up).
language_note: Investegate (the domestic RNS mirror) carried the primary documents the English wire summaries only paraphrase: the full 9M and H1 releases, the buyback completion schedule, the absence of Transaction in Own Shares since 28 May, the bond redemption, and BlackRock's TR-1 split between shares and CFDs.
Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: Sage is a FTSE 100 name with about 19 analysts, and the domestic retail press (Sharecast, Proactive, IC) is shut to both tools.
